seo_title: World clocks and calendar menu bar
seo_description: Free, open-source macOS menu bar clock with a month calendar, upcoming events, world clocks and a time-zone slider for planning calls. Native, offline.
hero_sub: ZoneClockBar turns the menu bar clock into a month calendar, event list and world clocks. Click it, then drag the slider to find a call time that works across cities.
features_sub: A small native app that keeps your date, events and teammates' local times one click away.

features.title: Configurable menu bar text
features.desc: Pick from 7 presets such as Tue 20 Oct 14:05 or write a custom date pattern, with a live preview. Pin any city's time next to the date.

features.title: Time-travel slider
features.desc: Drag up to 12 hours either way in 15-minute steps and every city updates together. Hours between 9 and 17 are shaded.

features.title: Month calendar popover
features.desc: Today is highlighted, with optional week numbers and a choice of first weekday. Arrow keys change month and T jumps back to today.

features.title: Upcoming events
features.desc: See events from the calendars you choose for the next 1 to 14 days, grouped by day with calendar colors. All-day and multi-day events are handled.

features.title: World clocks at a glance
features.desc: Each city shows local time, offset from your zone, a day offset like +1d and a sun or moon symbol. Click a city to copy its time.

features.title: Accurate and lightweight
features.desc: Refreshes on the minute, after wake from sleep, and when the system clock or time zone changes. A daylight saving marker appears when a city shifts within seven days.

permissions_step: When prompted, grant Calendar access (optional, only needed to show events) in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Calendars.

faq.q: Is ZoneClockBar really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is free to use and released under the MIT license, with the full source on GitHub. There are no ads, accounts or paid tiers, and an optional Ko-fi button is there if you want to support development.
Only read-only access to your calendars, used to list upcoming events. You can deny it and the clocks and calendar grid keep working. It asks for nothing else and makes no network connections.
Your clocks and settings are saved locally on your Mac in the app's preferences. Events are read from your calendars on demand and are never copied or sent anywhere.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
